lesson_title: The Conditions Are the Answer: Organic Reactions
hook_text: Same molecule. Same reagent. Two totally different products. The secret ingredient? The recipe on the label.
clip_script: Here is organic chemistry's best-kept exam secret: molecules do not choose their reactions — conditions do. Watch. Take 2-bromobutane and sodium hydroxide. Serve the hydroxide dilute, in water, gently warmed, and you get a polite swap: hydroxide taps the bromine on the shoulder and takes its exact seat. Substitution — out comes an alcohol. Now the SAME two chemicals, but concentrated hydroxide, dissolved in ethanol, at a rolling boil: the mood flips. A hydrogen gets ripped off the neighbouring carbon, the bromine storms out, and a double bond snaps into the gap. Elimination — out comes an alkene. Same partners, different lighting, different dance. And the double bond itself? It is a pair of open hands. Alkenes grab whatever you offer: hydrogen with a nickel catalyst turns oil into margarine; bromine loses its colour the instant those hands close — that is the classic alkene test. When the offer has two different pieces, remember the gossip rule: the rich get richer — the new hydrogen joins the carbon that already has more hydrogens. So read every question in this order: conditions first, molecule second, answer almost automatic. Hot concentrated acid means a double bond is coming. Light on an alkane means a swap. The exam prints the conditions because the conditions ARE the answer.
visual_style: A dance floor where the same two molecule characters switch routines as the lighting changes from calm blue to hot red; a double bond drawn as open hands grabbing bromine and draining its colour; condition labels stamped across the screen like passwords.
mood: Insider tip energy — handing over the cheat code to a feared topic.
pacing: One-two reveal of the same reagents giving two products, quick open-hands montage, punchy conditions-first close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and let the conditions answer Paper 2 for you.
